description: Pollo alla Cacciatora is a rustic and beloved Italian dish featuring tender chicken braised with tomatoes, bell peppers, onions, and often mushrooms and herbs. This hunter-style chicken stew is rich in flavor, combining savory and sweet notes from fresh vegetables and a robust tomato sauce. It is a comforting and hearty meal perfect for any family gathering, bringing the authentic taste of Italy to your table.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Pat chicken pieces dry and season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken in batches, skin-side down first, until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove chicken from the pot and set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics and Vegetables
instructions.text: Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onion to the pot and cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the chopped red and green bell peppers and sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables begin to soften.

instructions.title: Deglaze and Add Tomato Paste
instructions.text: Pour in the dry white wine (or chicken broth) and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon. Let the wine simmer for 1-2 minutes until slightly reduced. Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.

instructions.title: Combine with Tomatoes and Herbs
instructions.text: Add the crushed tomatoes and chicken broth to the pot. Stir well to combine all ingredients. Add the fresh rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.

instructions.title: Braise the Chicken
instructions.text: Return the seared chicken pieces to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure the chicken is mostly submerged. Cover the pot, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and tender. If the sauce becomes too thick, add a little more chicken broth.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Discard the rosemary, thyme stems, and bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley before serving. Pollo alla Cacciatora is excellent served with crusty bread, pasta, or creamy polenta.

tips: For the most flavor, use bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces. The skin renders fat and crisps up, adding depth, and the bones contribute to a richer sauce.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing the chicken or sautéing vegetables. Cook in batches if necessary to ensure even browning and prevent steaming.
Cacciatora pairs wonderfully with a variety of sides. Serve it with crusty Italian bread to soak up the delicious sauce, or alongside pasta, polenta, or mashed potatoes.
